parameters.subject: =[{{ $('Raise Hold Release Ops Approval').item.json.ref_code }}] FRAUD HOLD placed - account frozen, review needed
parameters.message:
=A transfer scored above the fraud threshold, so the account has been frozen automatically and no money moved.

Account ID: {{ $('Validate Request Payload').item.json.params.account_id }}
Amount attempted: Rs {{ ($('Validate Request Payload').item.json.params.amount / 100).toFixed(2) }}
Risk score: {{ $('Validate & Evaluate Fraud Decision').item.json.risk_score }} (threshold 75)
Decision: {{ $('Validate & Evaluate Fraud Decision').item.json.decision }}
Reason: {{ $('Validate & Evaluate Fraud Decision').item.json.reason }}

The customer cannot clear this themselves - by design, only a human can.

SIMILAR KNOWN PATTERNS (advisory - matched by similarity, NOT part of the score)
The freeze itself was decided by the deterministic rules above. The following is
background to help you judge, including the innocent explanations. It is not
evidence and it did not influence the decision to freeze.

{{ $json.pattern_block }}

HOW TO DECIDE
Reply to this email with a single word on the first line:

    APPROVE   - this was a legitimate transaction; release the freeze
or
    REJECT    - genuinely suspicious; leave the account frozen

Optionally add a line starting with NOTE: to record what you found.

Keep the reference {{ $('Raise Hold Release Ops Approval').item.json.ref_code }} in the reply - it is already in the subject line, so a normal reply works. Your reply must contain APPROVE or REJECT but not both. This reference expires in 7 days.

===BANKING-OPS-ACTION===
REF: {{ $('Raise Hold Release Ops Approval').item.json.ref_code }}
TYPE: fraud_hold_release
========================

nodes.notes: Queries the fraud_patterns namespace, never banking_policy. Set to continue on error on purpose: if the vector lookup is unavailable the ops alert must still go out. A missing advisory note is an inconvenience; a fraud freeze nobody is told about is a real problem.
